title: Braun Phonosuper SK 4 · Rams and Gugelot, 1956

subject.summary: The 1956 Braun Phonosuper SK 4 radio-phonograph: a white-lacquered steel box with elm side panels, its controls moved to the top deck under a raked clear acrylic hood, and the Wagenfeld PC 3 turntable inside. Modelled at 580 x 244 x 290 mm from published dimensions and three photographs.

sources.title: The owner's request
sources.ref: Masterpiece construct of a Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams and Hans Gugelot, 1956) plus a printable replacement for one missing large control knob.

facts.note: Presented autumn 1956 at 295 DM; the SK 4/1 revision followed in 1957.

facts.value: Hans Gugelot and Dieter Rams, with Wilhelm Wagenfeld's PC 3 turntable
facts.note: Gugelot: the white sheet-metal enclosure. Rams: the acrylic hood. Wagenfeld: the record player. Lindinger the controls, Aicher the scale (das programm).
58 cm in Die Neue Sammlung, V&A and das programm alike.
24.4 cm. V&A lists 29 cm depth for the later SK55; photo-1's front elevation (width 580 mm) puts the height at ~290 mm, which agrees with 24.4 cm depth and not with 29 cm.
29 cm over the closed hood. Traced check from photo-1: object height / width = 890/1754 px = 0.507 -> 294 mm.
Reported from Radiomuseum's data sheet; not weighed by the author.
White front panel from its bottom edge (y=0.021) to its top edge: 434 px at 3.02 px/mm = 144 mm.
The hood's back edge sits at the full 290 mm; its front edge meets the body's top at 144 mm over 244 mm of depth.

facts.value: White-lacquered sheet steel with punched speaker and vent slots
Rectangular cutout at the back of the hood for long-playing records overhanging the rear
All controls on the top deck, light grey: four small knobs in a column, a row of five push-buttons, one large tuning knob, one long dial scale
Five push-buttons labelled ein aus, Phono, LW, MW, UKW
Braun PC 3: idler drive, three speeds 33, 45 and 78 rpm, no changer, no counterweight
Three-arm platter support (star) around the spindle
facts.note: Wikipedia records that the three-nub support warped records left in the sun and that the SK 4/1 moved to five rubber pads.

facts.value: Isophon 170 x 250 mm elliptical speaker behind the front slots
ECC85, 2x EF89, EABC80, EL84; 3 W output

facts.note: Printed on the deck ahead of the dial.
Two blocks of unequal length on the front (and the same on the back), pitch 6.4 mm, slot 2.8 mm high.

authoring.provenance_note: Envelope 580x244x290 mm from Die Neue Sammlung, V&A and das programm; split, rake, grille bands, cheeks and layout measured on the three photographs. The back is inferred: no photo shows it. Lettering is a viewer overlay. The hood is one raked acrylic sheet with elm rails (photo-2's hinge corner). Round 12 of 12: critic 3,3,2,2,2,2,2,3,3, 8 items open; the round cap ended the run.

identity.feature: White-lacquered steel box with two unequal punched slot fields
Elm-cheeked sides raking up to carry the hood
One raked clear acrylic hood, elm rails, down-turned front lip, rear hinge
PC 3 platter with mat seam, label ring, three-arm clamp and spindle
Controls on the deck: four knobs, five keys, long scale, large Sender knob

next: The tonearm head is still a chamfered shoe rather than the PC 3's cast tapered pickup: a loft along the arm's last 40 mm would finish it.
The hero still holds the object at 41 per cent of the frame width; framing.fit 1.4-1.5 would fill it.
The back is inferred throughout; a photograph of an SK 4's rear would let the vent fields, type plate and inlet be drawn as evidence rather than placeholder.
The platter bay could drop 10 mm below the chassis plate, which needs the deck plate rebuilt as a frame rather than a slab.
A 10-inch record on the platter would match photo-1 and fill the turntable, but it is not on the owner's part list.
